source.title: Hidden not Deleted: How Networks Suppress Entangled Features
source.authors: Akash Samanta; M. Singh; Debasis Chaudhuri

page_placements.theme: Toy-model superposition geometry depends on sparsity, correlation, importance, loss, activation function and regularization

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a toy superposition model and reports experiments on how sparse, mutually exclusive features form antipodal shared representations. This bears on part of V3, but it does not measure polysemantic neurons in real networks.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the linear-erasure preservation sweep as a function of feature entanglement and the natural-emergence sweep for antipodal geometry. The paper does not measure whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, or how common such neurons are. Its excision, causal-patching, depth, GELU, and transformer results concern suppression and recovery, not the claim versions' neuron polysemanticity measures; citations to other work are not extracted as results. Table 1's representative values are not duplicated because Table 3 reports the full linear-baseline sweep.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Toy Model of Superposition as a testbed for concept erasure and unlearning. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to several unrelated inputs, how common such neurons are, or why. The TMS bottleneck h = W_E x is linear and has no privileged neuron basis, so its antipodal feature geometry is superposition in a representation space, not neuron polysemanticity. The linear-erasure sweep (Table 3) scores an erasure method's cost to feature A, which is the study's own method comparison. The natural-emergence sweep (Table 8, Figure 7) shows antipodal feature geometry arising with anti-correlation and a narrow bottleneck. That is a related construct, feature geometry rather than neuron response, and is recorded under fits_no_version. No version is tested, so no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that linear erasure fails on antipodally entangled features, increasingly so with entanglement. Gradient-based excision with a frozen encoder instead converges to one of two solutions, mirror or shadow, whose prevalence depends sharply on entanglement (crossover near rho -0.75). In both, the erased feature stays recoverable by a single scalar patch, so it is suppressed rather than deleted. They offer this as a candidate mechanism for LLM unlearning failures, limited to a toy setting.
record.recipe_differences: This is a toy-model concept-erasure study, not the original circuit-analysis or SoLU method, and it measures feature geometry and erasure outcomes rather than neuron response diversity.
record.method_sensitivity: Antipodal emergence varies with anti-correlation strength, sparsity, and bottleneck dimension. The reported linear-erasure preservation error increases with entanglement.

fits_no_version.finding: In TMS trained from scratch, a designated feature pair reaches antipodal encoder geometry (cos < -0.9) more often as anti-correlation rises: 0.068 at 0.00 to 0.562 under strict exclusivity. Emergence is near-certain with a small bottleneck and moderate-to-high sparsity, and rare with a wide bottleneck.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mutually exclusive sparse features come to share antipodal directions in superposition more often under stronger anti-correlation and narrower bottlenecks (feature geometry, not neuron polysemanticity).

record.problems: The experiments use synthetic toy networks and a designated feature pair, not individual-neuron response measurements in real vision or language models. The paper itself notes that the transformer check is small-scale and does not establish generality to production-scale language models. The natural-emergence sweep excludes non-converged runs, reports aggregate fractions without uncertainty intervals in Table 8, and the cell-level Figure 7 values are flattened in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1's three representative linear-erasure values duplicate the full sweep in Table 3. The main-text and appendix results on gradient excision, causal patching, architecture variants, and the transformer check address suppression/recovery rather than neuron polysemanticity; they are noted in gate_note but not recorded as rows. Appendix F's cell-level Figure 7 results are not extracted because the flattened figure text does not reliably support assigning every displayed value to its sparsity/dimension cell.

untested.parts: No vision models or neuron responses to images.
No measurement of MLP neuron polysemanticity in language models. The 2-layer transformer check uses synthetic tokens and studies suppression only.
No neurons are examined. Superposition is studied in a linear bottleneck, and the study does not link neuron polysemanticity to feature count exceeding neuron count.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
The ReLU/GELU and depth variants concern erasure basins, not the share of polysemantic neurons.
No analysis of whether neuron responses reflect one shared feature.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked V3 as tested and supports, but none of the measures concerns neurons. The TMS hidden layer is linear and has no neuron basis, and the erasure rows benchmark the study's own baseline method. All rows are relinked to none. The natural-emergence result is kept under fits_no_version as a superposition-geometry finding.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or vision-neuron responses are studied.
The transformer appendix uses synthetic token types and does not measure the share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts.

The experiments test feature entanglement and the emergence of antipodal shared geometry in a toy model, not whether individual neurons are polysemantic, how prevalent polysemantic neurons are, or whether feature count exceeds neuron count in the tested model.
No test of polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
Architecture and activation variants are assessed for erasure suppression outcomes, not for the share of polysemantic neurons or performance-preserving reduction of that share.
No investigation of whether mixed neuron responses share a coherent feature or job.
No comparison of neuron polysemanticity under alternative activation-range measurements or explanation-scoring methods.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Uses the TMS superposition setup as a tool and does not test any neuron polysemanticity version.

tranche.reason: Uses TMS superposition as a testbed for concept erasure. It never measures neuron-level polysemanticity: the bottleneck h = W_E x is linear and has no neuron basis. T4 fits, and T6 is also defensible.

source_check.notes: Table 8 fractions count only converged runs (10 seeds per cell before exclusions) and are marginalized over S and d. Per Figure 7, cells at anti-correlation 0 reach at most 0.30. Antipodal geometry stays rare at high sparsity with a wide bottleneck, even under strict exclusivity. This is feature geometry in a linear bottleneck, not a neuron measure.

statements.correction: Table 8: fraction of converged seeds with cos(wA,wB) < -0.9 is 0.068 at anti-correlation 0.00 and 0.562 at 1.00 (strict mutual exclusivity). Models trained from scratch with W_E free; values marginalized over sparsity and bottleneck dimension.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Toy-model feature geometry as anti-correlation increases
reader_labels.reason: The share of converged runs with antipodal geometry rises from 0.068 to 0.562 across anti-correlation strengths, and preservation damage under linear erasure grows with entanglement (r1–r20). These results support the superposition/overlap part of V3 in this toy setting, not its claim about polysemantic neurons generally.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Natural-emergence sweep marginalized over sparsity and bottleneck dimension
reader_labels.reason: Antipodal geometry reaches 0.562 under strict mutual exclusivity rather than appearing in nearly all runs; the authors also report that emergence varies with sparsity and dimension (r16–r20).
